out.corrected_sentence: I agree with you.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese non si dice 'io sono d'accordo' usando il verbo essere, ma si usa direttamente il verbo 'to agree'.

out.reply: That is a very common mistake, but don't worry! I am glad we are on the same page. What do you think about our topic today?

new_vocab.term: to be on the same page
new_vocab.translation_it: essere sulla stessa lunghezza d'onda / essere d'accordo
new_vocab.example: I am glad we are on the same page about the plan.

out.follow_up: Can you try to say 'I agree' in a full sentence about your favorite food?

out.corrected_sentence: I am 30 years old.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese non si usa il verbo 'avere' per l'età, ma il verbo 'essere'. Si dice 'I am 30'.

out.reply: Nice to meet you! So, how are you feeling today?

new_vocab.example: I am in my thirties.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me what you do for a living?

out.corrected_sentence: She doesn't like coffee.

corrections.explanation_it: Con la terza persona singolare (he, she, it) si usa 'does not' o la contrazione 'doesn't'.

out.reply: That is a common mistake, but don't worry! Do you prefer coffee or tea?

new_vocab.example: I prefer tea to coffee.

out.follow_up: Try to answer: Do you prefer coffee or tea?

out.corrected_sentence: Yesterday I went to the cinema with my friends.

corrections.explanation_it: Si usa il past simple 'went' perché l'azione è avvenuta ieri.

out.reply: That sounds fun! What movie did you see at the cinema?

new_vocab.example: I like to go out with my friends on weekends.

out.follow_up: Tell me about the movie!

out.corrected_sentence: I have lived here for two years.

corrections.original: I live here since two years
corrections.corrected: I have lived here for two years
corrections.explanation_it: In inglese, per un'azione che è iniziata nel passato e continua nel presente, si usa il Present Perfect. Inoltre, si usa 'for' per indicare la durata (due anni) e 'since' per indicare il momento preciso dell'inizio.

out.reply: That is great! How do you like living there so far?

new_vocab.example: How is your new job going so far?

out.follow_up: Can you tell me one thing you love about your city?

out.corrected_sentence: People are very friendly in my city.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese la parola 'people' è plurale, quindi richiede il verbo al plurale 'are'.

out.reply: That sounds lovely! I love visiting cities where the locals are welcoming.

new_vocab.example: The people in this village are very welcoming.

out.follow_up: What is the name of your city?

out.corrected_sentence: I want you to come with me.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese non si dice 'I want that you...', ma si usa la struttura 'want + persona + to + verbo'.

out.reply: I would love to go with you! Where are we going?

new_vocab.example: Can I go along with you?

out.follow_up: Can you try to use 'I want you to...' in a new sentence?

out.corrected_sentence: Can you explain this word to me?

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese il verbo 'explain' richiede la preposizione 'to' prima della persona a cui si spiega qualcosa.

out.reply: Of course! Which word would you like me to explain?

new_vocab.example: What does this word mean?

out.follow_up: Tell me the word you are thinking about.

out.corrected_sentence: I look forward to seeing you.

corrections.explanation_it: Dopo l'espressione 'look forward to', si usa sempre la forma in -ing perché 'to' è una preposizione.

out.reply: That is a very common mistake, but don't worry! I am also looking forward to our conversation.

new_vocab.example: I look forward to meeting you next week.

out.follow_up: Can you try to use 'look forward to' in a new sentence about your weekend?

out.corrected_sentence: I am very bored today.

corrections.explanation_it: Usa 'bored' per descrivere come ti senti (noioso/annoiato). 'Boring' significa che tu sei una persona noiosa.

out.reply: Oh, I am sorry to hear that. Why are you feeling bored today?

new_vocab.example: I am fed up with this rainy weather.

out.follow_up: What do you usually do when you are bored?

out.corrected_sentence: I have been here since Monday.

corrections.corrected: I have been here since Monday
corrections.explanation_it: In inglese, quando un'azione è iniziata nel passato e continua nel presente, si usa il Present Perfect (have been) invece del Present Simple.

out.reply: Oh, so you have been there for a few days now! How is your trip going so far?

new_vocab.example: How is your holiday going so far?

out.follow_up: Are you traveling for work or for pleasure?

out.corrected_sentence: He told me that he was tired.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese si usa 'tell' quando c'è un oggetto indiretto (me, you, him), mentre 'say' si usa per riportare le parole senza specificare subito a chi.

out.reply: I understand. It is common to confuse say and tell. Did he say why he was so tired?

new_vocab.example: Can you tell me a story?

out.follow_up: Can you try to use 'told' in a new sentence?

out.corrected_sentence: We discussed the project yesterday.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese il verbo 'discuss' è transitivo e non richiede la preposizione 'about'. Si dice 'discuss something'.

out.reply: That sounds interesting. What was the main topic of your discussion?

new_vocab.example: I want to bring up the budget during the meeting.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me one thing you decided during the meeting?

out.corrected_sentence: I'm going home now.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese non si usa la preposizione 'to' con la parola 'home' quando si usa con verbi di movimento come 'go'.

out.reply: That sounds good. Are you going home to relax or do you have some work to do?

new_vocab.example: I am tired, so I think I will head home now.

out.follow_up: What are you going to do when you get home?

out.corrected_sentence: My sister is taller than me.

corrections.explanation_it: Con gli aggettivi brevi di una sillaba come 'tall', si aggiunge il suffisso '-er' per fare il comparativo, non si usa 'more'.

out.reply: That is a very common mistake, but don't worry! How tall is your sister?

new_vocab.example: I am much shorter than my brother.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me how tall you are?

out.corrected_sentence: I ate pizza last night.

corrections.explanation_it: Il passato di 'eat' è irregolare: 'ate'. Inoltre, con un riferimento temporale specifico come 'last night', si usa il Past Simple e non il Present Perfect.

out.reply: That sounds delicious! What kind of pizza did you have?

new_vocab.example: The pizza was delicious.

out.follow_up: Tell me, what is your favorite topping on a pizza?

out.corrected_sentence: How many people were at the party?

corrections.explanation_it: Si usa 'how many' per i nomi numerabili come 'people', mentre 'how much' si usa per i nomi non numerabili.

out.reply: That sounds like a fun question. I am not sure, but I bet it was a great party. Was it a big celebration?

new_vocab.example: The party was very crowded.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me about the last party you attended?

out.corrected_sentence: I must finish this work today.

corrections.explanation_it: Dopo il verbo modale 'must' non si usa mai il 'to'. Si usa direttamente la forma base del verbo.

out.reply: That sounds like a busy day. Do you have a lot of tasks to complete?

new_vocab.example: I am very busy with my new project.
The deadline for this work is today.

out.follow_up: What kind of work do you do?

out.corrected_sentence: Last year I visited London.

corrections.explanation_it: Quando specifichi un momento preciso nel passato (come 'last year'), devi usare il Past Simple invece del Present Perfect.

out.reply: That sounds lovely! How long did you stay in London?

new_vocab.translation_it: fare il turista / vedere i monumenti
new_vocab.example: I went sightseeing in London last year.

out.follow_up: What was your favorite place in London?

out.corrected_sentence: I made a mistake in the exam.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese si usa il verbo 'make' con la parola 'mistake', non il verbo 'do'.

out.reply: Oh, I am sorry to hear that. Don't worry, everyone makes mistakes sometimes. What subject was the exam about?

new_vocab.example: I hope you pass the exam next time.
He was sad because he failed the exam.

out.follow_up: Was it a difficult exam?

out.corrected_sentence: I usually go to work by bus.
out.reply: That is a good way to travel. Do you have a lot of time to read or listen to music on the bus?

new_vocab.example: How long is your commute by bus?

out.follow_up: How long does your bus journey take?

out.corrected_sentence: We have been studying English for two years.
out.reply: That is great! You have already made a lot of progress. How do you usually practice your English?

new_vocab.example: You are making great progress with your English!

out.follow_up: Do you study with a teacher or by yourself?

out.corrected_sentence: She doesn't like spicy food.
out.reply: That is a perfect sentence. Do you like spicy food or do you prefer mild flavors?

new_vocab.example: I prefer mild salsa instead of hot sauce.

out.follow_up: Tell me about your favorite dish.

out.corrected_sentence: Could you tell me where the station is?
out.reply: Of course! I can help you with that. Are you looking for the train station or the bus station?

new_vocab.example: I am looking for the nearest pharmacy.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me which station you are looking for?

out.corrected_sentence: I'm looking forward to meeting your family.
out.reply: That is a very nice thing to say! Do you have any plans for the weekend?

new_vocab.example: I am looking forward to our next lesson.

out.corrected_sentence: Yesterday I went to the market with my brother.
out.reply: That sounds like a nice day. What did you buy at the market?

new_vocab.example: I need to go grocery shopping for the weekend.

out.follow_up: Did you buy any fresh fruit or vegetables?

out.corrected_sentence: i went to milan last week and it was great
out.reply: That sounds wonderful! What was your favorite thing to do in Milan?

new_vocab.example: I went sightseeing in Milan all day.

out.follow_up: Did you visit the Duomo or go shopping?

out.corrected_sentence: what time does the train leave
out.reply: That is a perfect question. Are you planning a trip by train soon?

new_vocab.example: The train is scheduled to depart at ten o'clock.
Which platform does the train leave from?

out.follow_up: Can you tell me what time your next train leaves?
